docs.title: Job Application Assistant
docs.text: A sophisticated multi-agent job application automation system built on Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK). This system automates the complete job application workflow: scraping jobs from multiple sites, creating Google Drive folders with resumes, generating tailored cover letters, and submitting applications.

docs.title: 🏗️ System Architecture
docs.text: User Input → Orchestrator Agent → Specialized Sub-Agents → Database & Google Drive

docs.title: Agent Hierarchy
docs.text:
orchestrator_agent (LlmAgent)
├── job_scraper_agent (scrapes from 5+ sites)
├── resource_manager_agent (creates folders, copies resumes)
│   └── batch_resource_manager (handles bulk folder operations)
├── content_generator_agent (analyzes fit, writes cover letters)
│   └── batch_content_generator (handles >25 jobs with rate limiting)
├── database_agent (database operations)
├── application_submitter_agent (automated submissions)
│   └── batch_submitter (sequential job applications)
└── email_assistant_agent (email classification)

docs.title: 🔑 Key Features
docs.text:
• Multi-Site Job Scraping: LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, Google Jobs
  • Smart Deduplication: Prevents duplicate applications across sites
  • Chrome Extension: Manual job saving from any website with one-click integration
  • Google Drive Integration: Automated folder creation and document management
  • AI Content Generation: Personalized cover letters using Gemini models And Resumes
  • Browser Automation: Headless job application submission with CAPTCHA solving
  • Email Classification: Process job-related emails automatically
  • Batch Processing: Handle large volumes with rate limiting

docs.title: 📚 Documentation
docs.text:
• Master Overview - Comprehensive system documentation
  • Chrome Extension Guide - Extension setup
  • Agent-specific documentation in each sub-agent folder

docs.title: Loading the Extension in Chrome
docs.text:
1. Open Chrome and navigate to chrome://extensions/
  2. Enable "Developer mode" (toggle in top right)
  3. Click "Load unpacked"
  4. Select the chrome-extension/dist folder
  5. The extension icon (JA) should appear in your toolbar!

docs.title: Testing the Extension
docs.text:
1. Visit a job listing on:
  2. LinkedIn (e.g., linkedin.com/jobs/view/...)
  3. Indeed (e.g., indeed.com/viewjob?...)
  4. Glassdoor

  5. ZipRecruiter

  6. Click the extension icon - you should see:

  7. "On Job Page" indicator
  8. Current job details extracted

  9. Save Job button

  10. Click "Save Job" to save it locally

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: npm install

docs.title: Development Mode (with hot reload)
docs.text: npm run dev

docs.title: Production Build
docs.text: npm run build

docs.title: 📁 Project Structure
docs.text:
chrome-extension/
├── dist/               # Built extension (load this in Chrome)
├── src/
│   ├── popup/         # Extension popup UI
│   ├── content/       # Content scripts for job extraction
│   └── background/    # Service worker for API calls
├── manifest.json      # Extension configuration
└── webpack.config.js  # Build configuration
  • ✅ Chrome extension structure with Manifest V3
  • ✅ Job extraction for LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter
  • ✅ Popup UI with job saving functionality
  • ✅ Local storage for saved jobs
  • ✅ Multi-site support with site-specific parsers

docs.title: Setting Up the Public Documentation Repository
Step 1: Create the Public Repo
docs.text:
1. Go to https://github.com/new
  2. Create a new repository:
  3. Name: job-application-assistant-docs
  4. Description: "Documentation for Job Application Assistant"
  5. Public (important!)
  6. DO NOT initialize with README, .gitignore, or license
  7. Click "Create repository"

docs.title: Step 2: Generate Deploy Keys
docs.text:
Run these commands in your terminal:

cd /home/dave/Desktop/job_application_assitant/docs-config

# Generate the deploy key pair (no passphrase - just press Enter twice)
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f job-docs-deploy-key -C "davidbzyk@gmail.com"

docs.title: Add Public Key to Public Repo:
docs.text:
1. Go to your new job-application-assistant-docs repo
  2. Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key
  3. Title: "Docs Deploy Key"
  4. Key: Copy contents of job-docs-deploy-key.pub
  5. Check "Allow write access"
  6. Add key

docs.title: Add Private Key to Private Repo:
docs.text:
1. Go to your private job_application_assistant repo
  2. Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
  3. New repository secret
  4. Name: ACTIONS_DEPLOY_KEY
  5. Value: Copy contents of job-docs-deploy-key (no .pub)
  6. Add secret

docs.title: Step 4: Set Up GitHub Actions
docs.text:
Create the workflow directory and copy the deploy file:

mkdir -p /home/dave/Desktop/job_application_assitant/.github/workflows
cp /home/dave/Desktop/job_application_assitant/docs-config/deploy-docs.yml /home/dave/Desktop/job_application_assitant/.github/workflows/

docs.title: Step 5: Update the Workflow
docs.text:
Edit .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml and update line 44 to use your GitHub username:

git clone git@github.com:YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/job-application-assistant-docs.git docs-public

docs.title: Step 6: Enable GitHub Pages on Public Repo
docs.text:
1. Go to the public job-application-assistant-docs repo
  2. Settings → Pages
  3. Source: Deploy from a branch
  4. Branch: gh-pages (will be created automatically)
  5. Folder: / (root)
  6. Save

docs.title: Step 7: Commit and Push
docs.text:
cd /home/dave/Desktop/job_application_assitant
git add .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml
git add docs-config/
git add README.md
git commit -m "feat: Add MkDocs documentation setup"
git push

docs.title: That's it!
docs.text: The GitHub Action will: 1. Trigger on push to main 2. Build the docs using MkDocs 3. Push to the public repo 4. GitHub Pages will serve them at: https://YOUR_USERNAME.github.io/job-application-assistant-docs/

docs.title: Note on Updates
docs.text:
The workflow only triggers when these files change: - Any README.md file - Files in docs-config/ - Files in ai-docs/ - The workflow file itself

This prevents unnecessary builds.
